title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Enterprise Tax Plan Base Rate Entities) Bill 2018
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Enterprise Tax Plan Base Rate Entities) Bill 2018

divisions.question: The majority voted against an amendment to the usual second reading motion, which is "*that the bill be read for a second time*" - parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill. This means it failed. ### Amendment text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words: "whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House:* > >> *(1) is of the opinion that with Government debt soaring ever higher, it's time the Turnbull Government abandoned its plan to give big business a multi-billion tax cut;* >> >> *(2) notes that the Government is debating legislative fixes that are a result of its slapdash approach to policy making; and* >> >> *(3) calls on the Government to commit to a post-implementation review of this measure".*

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (Enterprise Tax Plan Base Rate Entities) Bill 2017 as a "patch-up of a patch-up," but moved an amendment urging the Turnbull government to abandon its planned multi-billion-dollar tax cuts for big business and commit to a post-implementation review of the measure. The speech detailed ten alleged errors by Treasurer Scott Morrison, including the abandoned GST hike, negative gearing stance, false claims about tax avoidance laws, and the government's $65 billion corporate tax giveaway amid $501 billion gross debt.

speeches.speaker: Ted O'Brien
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Treasury Laws Amendment (Enterprise Tax Plan Base Rate Entities) Bill 2017 is necessary to maintain Australia's global competitiveness by introducing a passive income test for the lower 27.5% corporate tax rate, citing 403,000 new jobs created last year and warning that US corporate tax cuts to 21% could reduce Australia's GDP by 1% without similar reforms.

speeches.speaker: Julie Owens
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the government's belated attempt to fix a tax cut loophole for passive investment companies—known since 2016 but not addressed until seven months into the 2018 financial year—shows incompetence and created business uncertainty. The bill closes an unintended benefit from the government's centrepiece business tax cut, which the speaker noted would only increase wages by $2 per day in 20 years at a cost of $65 billion.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: The Treasury Laws Amendment (Enterprise Tax Plan Base Rate Entities) Bill 2017 clarifies criteria for the lower company tax rate, excluding businesses with more than 80% passive income and introducing a bright-line test effective from the 2017-18 income year.
